perModule.notes:
SURFACES 1 AND 2 GENUINELY DO NOT EXIST for this module, and that absence is itself the reason the MTC-class bug cannot occur here in its original form: there is no live profit preview at the POS to disagree with the stamp. It also means the operator has no in-module way to notice any of the seven divergences below — the first place a sales margin appears at all is the Profits page.

ROOT CAUSE OF DIVERGENCES 1, 2 AND 4 IS ONE RULE-14 VIOLATION. "Sales margin" is hand-written in five independent places with no shared fragment:
  packages/core/src/repositories/SalesRepository.ts:522   (item.price - costPrice) * item.quantity        [stamp]      qty YES  discount YES
  packages/core/src/repositories/ProfitRepository.ts:1268 si.sold_price_usd * si.quantity * weight        [profits]    qty YES  discount NO (revenue side)
  packages/core/src/repositories/ProfitRepository.ts:3066 (sold - cost) * si.quantity                     [pending]    qty YES  discount NO
  packages/core/src/repositories/ClosingRepository.ts:871 SUM(si.sold_price_usd - si.cost_price_snapshot_usd)          qty NO   discount NO
  packages/core/src/repositories/FinancialRepository.ts:130 same text                                                  qty NO   discount NO
  packages/core/src/repositories/SalesRepository.ts:1999   same text                                                  qty NO   discount NO
The last three are byte-identical copies of each other. Contrast this with the module's own gate predicates, which ARE properly extracted and shared (saleFullyPaid at ProfitRepository.ts:269, saleRecognitionWeight at :606, notRefunded at :636) — the gates were fixed by LIRA-160/161 and the VALUE expression was not. A single exported `saleMargin(saleAlias, itemAlias)` fragment would close divergences 1, 2 and 4 in one edit.

THE SECOND MTC-CLASS PATTERN (percentage over the wrong currency) IS NOT PRESENT HERE in its LBP form. Sales are USD-priced end-to-end (SalesRepository.ts:544-548 stamps amount_lbp = 0 by design), so `formatPct(row.profit_usd, row.revenue_usd)` at Profits.tsx:1356 always has a real USD denominator for the sales row — it can never show the 0% that the recharge row showed. It is wrong for a different reason (divergence 6: the denominator is pre-discount) and it silently ignores the LBP profit from kept change (divergence 3).

THINGS I CHECKED AND FOUND CLEAN — no divergence:
- Cost basis. The stamp reads `products.cost_price_usd` in a per-item SELECT (SalesRepository.ts:512-521) and `sale_items.cost_price_snapshot_usd` is written by a sub-SELECT of the SAME column in the SAME transaction (:762-765). No update can land between them, so snapshot == stamp basis. product_units has no cost column of its own (electron-app/create_db.sql:311-322), so the LIRA-143 IMEI/warranty work introduced no per-unit cost that could drift from the product-level one.
- Rule 13. SalesService.ts contains no SQL and no profit arithmetic (its only relevant method is a pass-through getChartData at :263). ProfitService assembles repository rows only.
- Refund/stamp symmetry on a WHOLE-sale refund. `_reversePayments` plus the negated stamp plus `is_refunded = 1` (TransactionRepository.ts:1702) net every surface to zero. The divergence is only on the PARTIAL item path.
- Currency conversion. No sales surface converts between USD and LBP, so there is no buy/sell-rate mismatch of the kind flagged for LIRA-174. (The closing PDF converts the AGGREGATE at sell_rate — frontend/src/features/closing/utils/rateStampedProfit.ts — but sales contribute $0 to the LBP side, so that conversion never touches sales money.)

ONE STALE COMMENT WORTH CORRECTING (not a divergence — I verified the code, not the comment). ClosingRepository.ts:1347-1359 states that `salesProfit` "still hand-inlines" saleFullyPaid's formula and lists exporting it as a follow-up. That is no longer true: line 876 calls `${saleFullyPaid("s")}` and the fragment is imported at line 25. The follow-up it describes is already done; the comment will mislead the next reader into "fixing" something that is fixed.

RANKING, if you want one fix first: divergence 1 (missing `* si.quantity`) is the highest-cost item. It is a silent, unbounded under-count on the document the owner files, it is undocumented anywhere in the repo, and it is a three-line change. Divergence 5 (ungated Dashboard arms) is the highest-cost OVER-count — it books profit on money that never arrived, which is the exact invariant profitRecognition.guard.test.ts exists to protect.

perModule.notes:
METHOD. Every claim below was read out of the source, and the arithmetic was checked against the LIVE application database (~/Documents/LiraTek/liratek.db) opened read-only through Python's stdlib sqlite3 (no better-sqlite3, no ABI coupling, no rebuild — per the handover's trap 6 and the memory note on the false-positive `require` probe). I edited nothing, ran no tests, builds, yarn/npm or Playwright.

THE ARCHETYPE IS PRESENT IN THE LIVE DB, EXACTLY AS DESCRIBED. recharges id=1: MTC, CREDIT_TRANSFER, amount 3, cost 255,000, price 300,000, currency_code LBP -> transactions id=11, profit_lbp 30,600, exchange_rate 89,000. exchange_rates: buy_rate 89,000, sell_rate 90,000, market_rate 89,500. 300,000 - 3x85,000 = 45,000; ceil(3/3)=1 message x $0.16 x 90,000 = 14,400; 45,000 - 14,400 = 30,600. A second row (Alfa $6 for 600,000 -> 61,200) reproduces it at 2 messages. Both figures are re-derived two ways: from the formula, and read straight out of the stamped rows.

RULE 14 CENSUS — the same "recharge margin" predicate is hand-written at SEVEN independent sites (ten literal occurrences), with no shared definition anywhere:
  1. frontend/src/features/recharge/components/TelecomForm.tsx:815-822 (preview value; again at :804-809 for the colour)
  2. frontend/src/features/recharge/components/TelecomForm.tsx:897-906 (PaymentSheet maxDiscount)

  7. packages/core/src/repositories/ClosingRepository.ts:1086, :1096, :1107, :1118 (four byte-identical copies inside one method, one per schema-degradation arm)
The SMS side, by contrast, IS centralised (packages/core/src/utils/telecomCredit.ts: SMS_TRANSFER_FEE_USD :30, planSmsTransfer :461-479) — but only the repository imports it. Everything in frontend/ is blind to it.

perModule.notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. Read-only; no tests, builds or package commands were run, per the brief. Every cite below was opened and read; I did not trust any doc comment about code without reading the code it describes, and that caught two stale comments (listed under "stale comments" below). The five surfaces all exist for this module — none is absent.

WHAT AGREES, PLAINLY. Three things I checked and found clean, so they are not padding the list. (1) The OMT commission MATH is identical on both sides today: the frontend's copied OMT_COMMISSION_RATES and both fee tier tables (Services/index.tsx:66-124) match packages/core/src/utils/omtFees.ts value for value, including the LBP INTRA formula max(50,000, ceil(amount/1,000,000)*10,000). The duplication is a drift channel (divergence 11), not a live wrong number. (2) The USD transaction-day path agrees end to end: for a model-1 row the stamp writes 0 (FinancialServiceRepository.ts:1966-1979), ProfitRepository's transaction-day arm reads that same 0 stamp (:1565), and Closing's legacy arm is gated to model-0 only (:972/:985/:1000) — the LIRA-158 interlock holds in USD. The LBP hole (divergence 3) is a currency problem, not a model problem. (3) The Services page's StatsCards chips are currency-correct (StatsCards.tsx:37-45 consumes getAnalytics's byCurrency arrays) — it is the Profits Commissions tab that ignores the same payload.

THE ARCHETYPE DOES NOT REPEAT HERE IN ITS EXACT FORM. There is no OMT/Whish equivalent of "the preview subtracts one cost and the stamp subtracts two". The OMT preview is honest — it computes the same fee x rate the backend computes and labels it an estimate. The closest structural match is divergence 9 (app-wallet Shop Profit shown gross while the submitted commission subtracts the discount), which is the MTC shape with a discount instead of an SMS fee.

MOST LIKELY TO BE WORTH THE OWNER'S TIME, in order: divergence 2 ($90,002.00 versus $2.00 + 90,000 LBP is an absurd number an operator would notice and could not reconcile), divergence 3 (LBP commission is invisible in the daily closing document, which is the report the shop closes on), divergence 1 (the module's own page overstates unearned LBP profit by roughly 90,000x in apparent dollars), divergence 4 (fresh, introduced 2026-09-05, and the exact class LIRA-159's own body warns about).

SURFACES I DELIBERATELY WENT BEYOND THE FIVE FOR, and why. The Dashboard "Monthly Net Profit" tile (FinancialRepository.getMonthlyPL:113-193) composes getRealizedCommissionTotals + getSupplierCommissionTotals, so it inherits divergence 6's definition rather than the Overview's stamp-based one — a sixth surface reporting a seventh number for the same money. I did not enumerate it as its own divergence because it is the same root cause as 6. The customer-session profit ledger is likewise outside the five but produced divergence 10.

TWO STALE COMMENTS FOUND WHILE VERIFYING (no numeric impact, but they will mislead the next reader). (a) FinancialRepository.ts:86-90 says it "Deliberately does NOT mirror ClosingRepository.getDailyStatsSnapshot's finProfitLegacy - that query is missing notPartnerPending/notDebtPending, a documented KNOWN GAP ... ticketed as LIRA-160." LIRA-160 shipped: both gates are present at ClosingRepository.ts:974, :986, :1000, :1003. (b) ClosingRepository.ts:49-51 says todayLocal "Mirrors the DATE(col,'localtime') = DATE('now','localtime') convention used across the reporting repositories (SalesRepository, FinancialServiceRepository)." SalesRepository does (:1627 et al.); FinancialServiceRepository.getAnalytics does not (:4728/:4746/:4760/:4778/:4793) — that is divergence 8.

ONE THING I COULD NOT SETTLE FROM CODE ALONE. Divergence 5 (Overview counts unsettled FS revenue, By-Date does not) is a recognition-basis question, not a bug with a right answer I can name. Both readings are defensible; what is indefensible is one page answering it twice. It needs the owner, in the same way LIRA-173 needed an interview.

WHAT I DID NOT COVER. I did not audit the REST twins in backend/src/api for envelope or gating parity on these queries, and I did not check the web-mode renderer — the brief scoped this to locating and comparing the five surfaces. I also did not verify divergence 12 against a fixture (its own caveat says so); it is the one entry on the list I would call Likely rather than Certain. Everything else on the list is re-derived from code I read at the cited lines.

perModule.notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. Every cite below was opened and read; I did not trust any comment about code over the code itself, and I re-checked the two claims the whole report leans on. (1) `custom_services.profit_usd` really is a generated column on BOTH schema paths — `electron-app/create_db.sql:892-893` for a fresh DB and `packages/core/src/db/migrations/index.ts:549-550` for a migrated one. This mattered: if the migrated path had a plain column, the INSERT at CustomServiceRepository.ts:144-171 (which does not list profit_usd) would leave it 0 and the finding would have been a far larger bug instead of a drift. It is generated on both. (2) kept change genuinely reaches the repository on both transports — `kept_change_usd/lbp` are present in the core validator (validators/customService.ts:25-26) AND in the hand-duplicated desktop schema (electron-app/schemas/index.ts:803-804, which is explicitly labelled a rule-14 local duplicate). Had it been missing from the desktop copy, Zod would strip it and divergence 1 would be web-only.

ROOT CAUSE, STATED ONCE. `profit = price - cost` for this module exists in four independent, hand-maintained definitions: the SQL generated column (create_db.sql:892-893), the JS stamp expression (CustomServiceRepository.ts:259-266), the React preview (index.tsx:296-297), and — implicitly — the closing arm's choice to sum the generated column rather than the stamp (ClosingRepository.ts:1181). Divergence 1 is what happens when one of four copies grows a term. Divergences 2, 3, 4 and 5 are the same shape applied to the *gates* around that number (currency split, partner coverage, refund/void, business day) rather than the number itself. There is no single named definition of "custom-service profit" anywhere in the codebase to point a fix at; ProfitRepository's `notRefunded` / `notDebtPending` / `notPartnerPending` / `dateRange` fragments show the pattern the module should have followed.

WHAT I DID NOT FIND. The VIA-partner mode is clean: it books a `THROUGH_CUSTOM_SERVICE` partner_ledger CREDIT (CustomServiceRepository.ts:589-612) whose transaction_type does not match the `FOR\_%` pattern used by both partnerCoverageRatio (:381) and notPartnerPending (:293), so it correctly recognises immediately on every surface and stamps price-cost like a walk-in. The debt gate is consistent — `notDebtPending` is applied identically in the Profits arm (:1732) and the closing arm (:1183) and is keyed on the same `Custom Service Debt` charge type (:412). The exchange_rate stamped on the row does not enter any profit formula (every surface is per-currency, nothing converts), so the MTC-class "one surface uses a different rate" defect does not exist here. Refunds net correctly in the generic per-user/per-client arms because the REFUND row negates the stamp.

TWO SMALLER THINGS THAT DID NOT EARN A DIVERGENCE ENTRY (no worked example with two user-visible numbers). (a) `exchange_rate` is sent by the form (index.tsx:376-380) but is absent from the desktop IPC schema `CustomServiceCreateSchema` (electron-app/schemas/index.ts:775-820) while present in the core/web one (validators/customService.ts:46) — so on desktop Zod strips it and the repository falls back to the live snapshot rate. It changes the rate stamped on the transaction row for display, not any profit figure, so no two surfaces disagree on money. (b) getByUser/getByClient have no `cs.status = 'completed'` gate, so a `status: 'pending'` custom service would contribute profit there but not in By-Module or the closing snapshot. The current UI never sends `status` (the payload at index.tsx:370-415 omits it, so the schema default 'completed' applies), so it is unreachable from the app today — a latent drift, not an observable one.

SURFACES I COULD NOT LOCATE: none. All five exist for this module. The "table" surface has two distinct halves (per-row history modal and the Today's-* cards) reading the same generated column through different queries; I recorded both under the one entry because they share the formula and disagree with each other only via the gates already reported in divergences 4 and 5.

UNRELATED ENVIRONMENT NOTE: this session reported that the claude.ai Gmail and Sentry MCP connectors need authorization and cannot be authorized from a non-interactive session. Neither was needed for this audit.

METHOD / LIMITS. Read-only, as instructed: I ran no tests, builds, yarn, npm or Playwright, and edited nothing. Every claim below is from source read this session; I re-opened each cited line rather than trusting a comment about it, since two of this repo's own comments turned out to disagree with the code (CheckoutModal.tsx:45-49 asserts Maintenance may not show the keep-change button, while index.tsx:841 sets allowKeepChange={true}; ClosingRepository.ts:1210-1216 states maintProfit needs only the notDebtPending axis, which is true for the gates but silently leaves the USD-only margin expression unexamined). Required reading done: CLAUDE.md (rules 13/14/18 in particular), docs/HANDOVER_2026-09-04.md section 4, current_sprint.md at the repo root (NOT docs/tickets/CURRENT_SPRINT.md).

THE MTC ARCHETYPE DOES NOT EXIST HERE, AND CANNOT. The prompting bug was a live preview formula racing a stamp formula. Maintenance has no live profit preview at all (surface 1) and no profit/cost/margin column in its own history (surface 2) — verified by reading both files end to end, not by grep alone. The operator can enter a Repair Cost and a Price to Client and is never shown the difference, anywhere in the module. That absence is itself worth reporting: nothing in the maintenance UI would let an operator notice divergences 1, 3, 5 or 7. Whatever the closing PDF prints is the first and only number they see.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY CLEAN. The three surfaces that DO read the stamp agree exactly. getMaintenanceTotals (ProfitRepository.ts:1751-1776), getByDate's daily_maint (:2405-2423) and the ProfitService summary/module assembly (ProfitService.ts:449-501, :601-614) are per-currency throughout, apply the same five gates, and never convert LBP into USD. The v101 backfill (migrations/index.ts:4149-4162) is per-currency and correct for its era. maintenanceCompleted (ProfitRepository.ts:970-972) is genuinely shared between ProfitRepository and ClosingRepository (imported at ClosingRepository.ts:21) — that particular rule-14 debt was already paid, and its doc comment records why. Maintenance has no partner-routing path, and correctly carries no partnerCoverageRatio in any query. Refund symmetry is correct: the REFUND row carries the negated stamp (TransactionRepository.ts:1614-1633), `Maintenance Debt` is classified in notDebtPending's list (ProfitRepository.ts:406), and _cancelDebt covers it. The session-basket path is sound — SessionCheckoutService.ts:117 injects deferPayment: true, and processPayments returns before the drawer/change/debt block (MaintenanceRepository.ts:457-460) while still stamping full profit.

TWO THINGS I FOUND AND DELIBERATELY DID NOT FILE AS DIVERGENCES, so you know they were looked at:
1. getByUser/getByClient compute `revenue_lbp` as a bare `SUM(t.amount_lbp)` with no CASE and no debt gate (ProfitRepository.ts:2817, :2973) while every other column on those rows is gated — the method's own doc acknowledges it (ProfitRepository.ts:2716-2718). For an LBP maintenance job charged entirely to CUSTOMER_ACCOUNT the arithmetic diverges (By Cashier revenue_lbp 300,000 vs By Module revenue_lbp 0), but I could not make it user-visible: neither the By Cashier nor the By Client table declares a revenue_lbp column (Profits.tsx:1692-1700, :1760-1769), and DataTable's export is driven by the declared columns (packages/ui/src/components/ui/DataTable.tsx:567-569, :679-686), so it never reaches an operator's screen or export. Latent, not live.
2. The History modal's \"Price\" column declares `sortKey: \"price_usd\"` (HistoryModal.tsx:159) while the cell renders price_lbp for LBP rows — so sorting by Price files every LBP job under 0. Same class as LIRA-139's Amount-column fix. Cosmetic ordering, no number is wrong, so it is a follow-up rather than a divergence.

CROSS-REFERENCES TO THE LIVE BOARD. Divergence 1 is the maintenance answer to the module-by-module verification LIRA-176 explicitly asks for (current_sprint.md:3593-3615: \"Reported but NOT yet verified ... maintenance ... the mechanism may differ per module (some may only ever have USD columns, which would be a non-issue rather than a gap)\"). For maintenance it is a real gap — the columns, the UI toggle and the stamp are all genuinely LBP-capable. Divergence 1 also converts LIRA-174's \"(Loto only)\" PDF label from a conservative hedge into a documented understatement. Divergences 3 and 7 are LIRA-160's unfinished half: that ticket added the gates to maintProfit but left the USD-only, source-recomputed margin expression untouched.

RANKING, if only one thing gets fixed: switch ClosingRepository's maintProfit to JOIN transactions and sum t.profit_usd/t.profit_lbp, contributing the LBP slice to totalProfitLBP. That one change closes divergences 1, 3 and 7 at once and removes the second hand-written copy of the margin. Divergence 5 (the dropped kept_change_*) is the only one where cash physically leaves the accounting model, so it is the highest per-incident cost even though it is rarer; note that fixing 5 before 7 actively widens 7.

SELF-ATTACK. The input that would flip the most here is my reading that `buildPricing` (index.tsx:186-206) really does zero the unselected currency's columns on every write path — if any path let cost_usd and cost_lbp be non-zero simultaneously, the stamp would drop one of them and divergence 1's arithmetic would change shape. I traced all four writers (buildPricing at :186, handleSaveDraft at :351, handleCheckoutComplete at :394, handleStatusTransition at :251) and each either calls buildPricing or forwards already-zeroed stored values, so the invariant holds today; it is not enforced by a constraint or a guard test, though, and nothing would stop a future caller from breaking it. Second: divergence 3's reachability rests on isPaymentComplete(0, 0) being true and on no other guard blocking a zero-payment checkout — I verified both (paymentUtils.ts:115-118; CheckoutModal.tsx:468-516) but did not execute it, so treat the reachability as Likely rather than Certain while the divergence between the two queries is Certain regardless of how the state is reached. Divergence 2's premise that repairs routinely span days is supported by the module's own design (four pre-delivery statuses, a draft button, a transition button) and by current_sprint.md:1316 describing exactly that lifecycle, but I have no production data on how often it actually happens.

perModule.notes:
SURFACE 1 DOES NOT EXIST — that is itself the first finding. The Loto sell form never shows the operator a commission figure before submit. `commissionAmount` is computed (index.tsx:112-114) and put in the payload (:261), but it is stripped by zod (`lotoSellSchema` has no such key) and recomputed server-side (LotoService.ts:157). So there is no MTC-shaped preview-vs-stamp bug here for the simple reason that there is no preview; the nearest thing the operator sees is the header "Commission" stat card, which is today's TOTAL, not this ticket's. Note the asymmetry though: `commission_rate` IS accepted from the client (validators/loto.ts:30) and takes precedence over settings — see the last divergence.

WHAT IS GENUINELY CLEAN. getLotoTotals (ProfitRepository.ts:1787-1808) and the `daily_loto` CTE (:2424-2437) are byte-for-byte the same query modulo the GROUP BY — same partnerCoverageRatio weighting, same three gates, same date column. The Profits Overview card and the By Module row both come from that single method through ProfitService (:407 and :621), so they cannot disagree. LOTO_CASH_PRIZE, LOTO_MONTHLY_FEE and LOTO_SETTLEMENT stamp no profit at all (LotoCashPrizeRepository.ts:79-93, LotoMonthlyFeeRepository.ts:101-115, LotoCheckpointRepository.ts:278-296) and none of those types is in PROFIT_TXN_TYPES (ProfitRepository.ts:953-954), so there is no double-count between the sale and its settlement. The refund path negates both profit columns symmetrically (TransactionRepository.ts:1613-1633).

TWO THINGS I FOUND BUT DID NOT FILE AS DIVERGENCES, because no two surfaces disagree — every surface omits them identically:
- The loto MONTHLY FEE is a genuine cost that reaches no profit surface at all. It debits the drawer (LotoMonthlyFeeRepository.ts:107,117-120) and lands in `loto_monthly_fees`, not `expenses`, so `activeExpense`-gated expense arms never see it. The module's own settlement math DOES subtract it ("We owe LOTO: sales minus our commission, plus any fees", LotoService.ts:326,338) — so the loto settlement view and every profit view disagree about whether the fee is a cost, but the profit views are uniformly silent, not inconsistent with each other.
- `notRefunded` (retroactive removal, used by getLotoTotals) versus REFUND-row netting (used by getByUser/getByClient) gives different answers when the sale and its refund fall in different reporting periods. This is a documented app-wide pattern (ProfitRepository.ts:1817-1823 spells out the same tradeoff for PM fees), not loto-specific, so I left it out.

ONE COSMETIC BUG NOT WORTH A TICKET ON ITS OWN: TicketHistoryModal's Date column declares `sortKey: "sale_date"` (:171) but renders `created_at` (:218-223). With the sale_date/created_at split described in divergence 6, a backdated ticket displays one date and sorts by another.

METHOD / CONFIDENCE. Every file:line above was read in this session and re-checked with `sed -n` after drafting; none is quoted from a comment. Where a comment and the code disagreed I trusted the code and said so — ClosingRepository.ts:1250-1253's "mirrors getLotoTotals verbatim ... notPartnerPending" is false as of commit 5d61f9a4, which is precisely the class of stale cite the brief warned about. The one claim I could NOT execute against a live database is the SQLite behaviour of the inverted `BETWEEN '2026-09-07' AND '2026-09-06'` range in divergence 7 case A; I am reading it from the SQL text (LotoTicketRepository.ts:461) plus the backend's own comment naming that exact failure (LotoService.ts:620-621), and standard SQL semantics make an inverted BETWEEN match nothing. Likely, on that basis: zero rows. The refund half of that same divergence (case B) needs no such inference and stands on its own. I also did not verify divergence 10's precondition (a real settings-fetch failure) — the code path is plainly there, but I did not reproduce it. I ran no tests, builds or package commands, and made no edits.

perModule.notes:
WHAT IS ACTUALLY CLEAN — worth stating plainly, because most of this module is:

1. The dominant path (USD<->LBP, no lot, no partner) is byte-identical across preview, stamp, Profits and Closing. The preview total is `effectiveResult.totalProfitUsd`, submit sends that same value (index.tsx:951), `_applyExchangeLotEffects` returns `touched:false` for a USD/LBP pair before any rate lookup (ExchangeRepository.ts:686-689), so `exchange_transactions.profit_usd` and `transactions.profit_usd` are the previewed number unchanged. No MTC-style missing cost term exists on this path.

2. The frontend does NOT hand-roll the profit arithmetic. It imports `calculateExchange` and `computeOverrideLegProfitUsd` from @liratek/core (index.tsx:32-33) — the same functions the server-side `ExchangeService.addTransaction` would use. That is the single biggest reason exchange does not have the MTC bug: the formula genuinely has one owner (packages/core/src/utils/currencyConverter.ts).

3. The FIFO walker is shared: `consumeFifo` and `previewConsume` both delegate to one private walker (ExchangeLotRepository.ts:384-537, doc at :384-386). The lot-adjusted numbers are computed once and stamped on both the exchange row and the unified row from the same variable (ExchangeRepository.ts:342-357 then :408).

4. Dual-transport parity holds. Both electron-app/handlers/exchangeHandlers.ts:50 and backend/src/api/exchange.ts:70 call `ExchangeService.addDirectTransaction` against the one shared `exchangeSubmitSchema` (packages/core/src/validators/exchange.ts:78-95). `ExchangeService.addTransaction` (which recomputes from DB rates and would silently discard operator rate overrides) is now unreferenced by either transport — dead as a production path, but still exported and still a live footgun for a future caller.

5. Rule 20 is satisfied: TransactionRepository refuses to void an exchange whose lots are not reversible (`_assertExchangeLotsVoidable`, :1335-1338, :1571-1572) and restores FIFO consumption on both the refund and the void path (`_reverseExchangeLotEffects`, :1440, :1677). Profits and Closing both read `exchange_transactions.is_refunded`, so a reversed exchange drops out of both — no double-count, no orphan.

6. Closing's missing `notDebtPending` is a real non-issue, verified rather than assumed: ExchangeRepository.ts:504-513 hard-rejects any non-drawer payout method (`isDrawerAffectingMethod`), so an exchange can never write a CUSTOMER_ACCOUNT debt row. The comment at ClosingRepository.ts:1296-1301 is right about that half; it is wrong only about the partner half (divergence 2).

CAVEATS AND LIMITS OF THIS AUDIT:

- Everything above is source-read only, as instructed. I ran no tests and queried no database, so nothing here is confirmed against live rows. In particular I did not verify that any for-partner exchange with PARTIAL settlement coverage actually exists in the owner's DB — divergence 2 is proven reachable from code (PartnerRepository.applySettlementCoverage:424-469 writes partial `covered_amount`; ExchangeRepository.ts:576-593 books the FOR_EXCHANGE row) but its current live incidence is unknown.
- Divergence 3 (NO_RATE_ANCHOR) is the narrowest: it needs a cross where BOTH sides are non-LBP exotics with no `exchange_rates` row AND an operator rate override. I confirmed each precondition is individually reachable in the UI but did not confirm the owner actually trades such pairs.
- Divergence 1's severity assumes `formatAmount(row.revenue_usd, "USD")` renders a plain currency figure; I read the call site (Profits.tsx:1345) but not `formatAmount`'s body.
- Assumption (unverified): `getDecimals("EUR")` returns 2 in divergence 4's worked example. I traced the call (index.tsx:660-661, :685-686) but not the hook's table. The divergence exists for any non-zero rounding; only the exact cent figure depends on this.
- Surfaces I looked for and did NOT find: the Exchange page has no "today's profit" stats card (`getTodayStats`, ExchangeRepository.ts:975-1001, returns totalIn/totalOut/count only and has no renderer in the page). PositionsPanel's `unrealized_profit_usd` (ExchangeLotService.ts:222-246) is explicitly display-only and deliberately never reaches ProfitRepository — I do not count it as a divergence.
- One thing I noticed but did not chase because it is an amount, not a profit: `transactions.amount_usd` on an LBP->X or X->LBP cross exchange is overwritten with the leg-1 PROFIT rather than an amount (ExchangeRepository.ts:383 and :396, both self-documented as "informational"). Anything that sums `transactions.amount_usd` across types — the Transactions viewer's amount column and LIRA-139's amount sort — is reading a profit as a transaction size for those rows.

perModule.notes:
WHAT AGREES — stated plainly, because it is most of the module. The four reporting reads of the `expenses` table are in genuine, textual agreement and I found no arithmetic difference between them: ProfitRepository.getExpenseTotals (:1873-1886), ProfitRepository's daily_expenses CTE (:2438-2447), ClosingRepository.expensesStats (:855-865) and FinancialRepository.getMonthlyPL's expenses block (:160-174) all call the SAME activeExpense() fragment, all bound the date on datetime/DATE(expense_date,'localtime'), all sum amount_usd and amount_lbp as independent per-currency figures, and all net them per-currency with no conversion (ProfitService.ts:515-516, ProfitRepository.ts:2485-2486, FinancialRepository.ts:186-188). There is no cost the expense arm subtracts that another does not, and no rate applied on one side and not the other. The MTC archetype's exact shape — a hand-rolled preview formula competing with a repository formula for the same profit concept — does not occur here for profit, because expenses carry no profit: the stamp writes profit_usd = profit_lbp = 0 (TransactionRepository.ts:515-516) and no surface reads it. Every divergence above is in the module's own page or in a presentation layer, not between the money queries.

A SIXTH SURFACE, outside the five you named: the Dashboard's monthly net-profit tile. FinancialRepository.getMonthlyPL (:160-188) → Dashboard.tsx:388, :396-397, :855-856. It is gated identically to the Profits page and I found no divergence in it, but it is a second net-profit-after-expenses figure on a different screen and belongs on any map of this module.

MODULE-PAGE DEFECTS THAT ARE NOT TWO-SURFACE DIVERGENCES, so I did not file them above:
1. HistoryModal.tsx:203 renders the literal string "Cash" in the "Paid By" column for every row. paid_by_method IS projected (ExpenseRepository.ts:95) and IS on the interface (HistoryModal.tsx:13). A Line_Usage expense (paid_by_method 'LINE_CREDIT', which moved a carrier credit drawer, not cash — CarrierLineRepository.ts:906, ExpenseRepository.ts:174-182) and a BINANCE expense (which moved USDT, ExpenseRepository.ts:192-197) both display as "Cash". Same class as the LIRA-119/121/122/129/131 family the sprint board calls out at current_sprint.md:729-733: money correct, screen wrong.
2. The History modal can only ever show today. It is passed `expenses` (Expenses/index.tsx:311), which is getTodayExpenses' output, and its DateRangeFilter is a client-side filter over that array (HistoryModal.tsx:40-43 → useDateRangeFilter.ts:14-22) — from/to can only narrow, never widen. A figure on the Profits or Closing surface for any prior day cannot be reconciled against the module's own history at all. There is no getExpensesByDateRange method on the repository.
3. Its export buttons are labelled exportFilename="expenses-history" (HistoryModal.tsx:156) and export the same today-only rows.

THE ARCHETYPE'S SECOND CLASS (margin from the wrong currency) — present on the Profits page but NOT on an expenses row. Profits.tsx:1356 computes the By-Module Margin column as formatPct(row.profit_usd, row.revenue_usd) (helper at :291), USD columns only, on a table whose rows include LBP-native modules. LOTO is the clean case: ProfitService.ts:619-630 pushes revenue_usd: 0 and profit_usd: 0 with all the money in the LBP fields, so a loto row showing 450,000 LBP profit on 5,000,000 LBP revenue renders Margin from 0/0 — exactly the 0%-on-a-real-margin symptom in your brief. I am reporting it only as context: expenses have no By-Module row at all (see the getByModule finding), so this specific cell can never be an expenses cell. It belongs to whoever audits loto / mobile services.

VERIFICATION METHOD AND CAVEATS. Every line cite above was read from the file in this session, not from a comment about the file; where a comment and the code disagreed I followed the code (e.g. PostRefactorVerification.test.ts:1499's title says getTodayExpenses "uses DATE(created_at)" — it uses expense_date). The SQLite date arithmetic in divergences 2 and 3 I executed rather than reasoned about, using Python's stdlib sqlite3 (3.50.4, zero ABI coupling per the handover's trap 6 — no build, no rebuild, nothing that could disturb desktop e2e): DATE('2026-09-05T00:00:00.000Z') = '2026-09-05' and datetime('2026-09-05T00:00:00.000Z','localtime') = '2026-09-05 03:00:00' on this UTC+3 machine. One caveat carried forward: LIRA-168 (handover §4 item 5) records that under core jest on Windows, SQL 'localtime' resolves to +1 while JS resolves to +3 — that would change the WIDTH of divergence 2's nightly window in a test fixture, not its existence, since the two predicates differ textually in any non-UTC zone. I ran no tests, builds, yarn, npm or Playwright, and changed no file.

I located all five surfaces; none was missing. The one partial absence is surface 4: ProfitService.getByModule (ProfitService.ts:528-679) has no expenses arm, so the Profits "By Module" tab omits the module even though the Summary and By-Date tabs both deduct it — filed as its own consequence inside the By-Date finding rather than as a separate divergence, because nothing there displays a WRONG number, a row is simply absent.

RANKING, if you are filing tickets: divergence 1 (is_refunded gap) first — it is live today, needs one line, and ExpenseActiveGate.test.ts already holds the two-door fixture to extend for rule 17. Then divergence 6 (split-mode preview), which is the true MTC-class defect here and the only one that can make the operator confirm one amount and book another. Then 4 (LBP vanishing from the Daily tab). Divergences 2, 3 and 7 travel together with 1 in the same file. Divergence 5 needs an owner decision before any code moves.

confirmed.title: Closing PDF, Dashboard monthly tile and Dashboard profit chart all drop `* si.quantity` — a multi-unit line contributes ONE unit's margin
confirmed.detail: The stamp multiplies by quantity (packages/core/src/repositories/SalesRepository.ts:522 `saleProfitUsd += (item.price - costPrice) * item.quantity`) and every ProfitRepository sales query does too (:1268, :1269, :2311, :2312, :3066). Three other queries sum the bare per-unit difference with no quantity factor: packages/core/src/repositories/ClosingRepository.ts:871, packages/core/src/repositories/FinancialRepository.ts:130 (getMonthlyPL → Dashboard "Monthly Net Profit" tile, frontend/src/features/dashboard/pages/Dashboard.tsx:388,396), and packages/core/src/repositories/SalesRepository.ts:1999 (getChartData("Profit") → Dashboard "Profit Trend (Last 30 Days)", Dashboard.tsx:383,1289). `sold_price_usd` and `cost_price_snapshot_usd` are UNIT values, not line totals — proven at SalesRepository.ts:901-911, which binds `item.price` into `sold_price_usd` while `quantity` goes into its own column.
confirmed.workedExample:
One cart line: 3 x phone case @ $10, product cost $6 each, no discount, $30 cash tendered.

  Closing PDF:           SUM(10 - 6) over 1 row  =  $4.00

confirmed.suspectedAuthority: The stamp and ProfitRepository are correct. They agree with each other, they carry the quantity factor the schema requires, and the sale value they reconcile against (final_amount_usd = $30) is only consistent with $12 of margin at a $18 cost. The three bare-difference copies are wrong. Not documented as a known gap anywhere: grep for `si.quantity` across docs/ and current_sprint.md returns nothing, and profitRecognition.guard.test.ts never mentions quantity.
corrections:
The claim stands as filed — arithmetic, magnitude, line cites, authority and consumer surfaces all verified. Three refinements worth folding into the ticket, none of which change the conclusion:

1. SCOPE LIMIT THE CLAIMANT OMITTED (most important). IMEI/unit-tracked lines are hard-pinned to quantity = 1 by a BusinessRuleError at packages/core/src/repositories/SalesRepository.ts:854 ("unit-tracked lines are one-unit-per-line"), so phone sales cannot trigger this. The divergence bites only non-unit-tracked stock — accessories, cases, consumables — which is exactly the worked example. This narrows blast radius (and likely explains why it went unnoticed: the highest-value SKUs are immune) but does not affect the arithmetic.

2. A FOURTH AUTHORITY SITE THE CLAIMANT MISSED, which strengthens the case: the refund reversal at packages/core/src/repositories/SalesRepository.ts:1413-1414 computes `(item.sold_price_usd - item.cost_price_snapshot_usd) * params.refundQuantity`. So the tally is 4 quantity-carrying sites vs 3 bare — and it means a refund's NEGATIVE stamp is quantity-scaled while closing's POSITIVE is not, so a fully-refunded multi-unit line drives the closing/monthly/chart figures NEGATIVE rather than to zero. Worked example: the 3-unit line fully refunded contributes +4.00 at sale and -12.00 at refund on those three surfaces, netting -8.00 where it must net 0. That is a second, arguably worse, symptom worth naming in the ticket.

3. TWO MINOR CITE LOOSENESSES. (a) "proven at SalesRepository.ts:901-911" — :901-909 is the .run() binding; the INSERT column list that actually establishes the ordering is at :763-767, and the cost binding is the subquery at :766. Cite both. (b) Dashboard.tsx:1289 is the `{ value: "Profit", label: "Profit" }` select option, not the chart render; the load call is :383.

Suggested fix direction (all three sites take `* si.quantity`), with the rule-14 observation that this is precisely the copy-paste-a-predicate failure mode rule 14 exists to prevent: the sales-margin expression should be ONE named fragment beside saleFullyPaid/notRefunded in ProfitRepository.ts's rule-14 block and reused, not a seventh hand-written copy. Per rule 17, prove any guard test fails on the pre-fix code first.

The claim stands as written. Three refinements for the ticket body, none of which weaken it:

1. SCOPE NARROWING (blast radius). SalesRepository.ts:829-855 rejects `item.quantity !== 1` on any line carrying a `product_unit_id`, and current_sprint.md:2057-2058 records the rule: "Unit-tracked cart lines are quantity-1 (one unit per line; selling 3 phones = 3 lines)." So IMEI/unit-registered goods — phones — cannot trigger this. The divergence is confined to non-unit-tracked products sold with quantity > 1: accessories, cases, chargers, SIMs. The claimant's phone-case example is exactly right, but the ticket should say the defect cannot affect unit-tracked inventory.

2. A SECOND DIVERGENCE IN THE SAME THREE QUERIES, unmentioned. The stamp also subtracts the sale-level discount at SalesRepository.ts:530 `saleProfitUsd -= sale.discount || 0` (rationale at :492-495: the discount comes out of margin). None of ClosingRepository.ts:871, FinancialRepository.ts:130, or SalesRepository.ts:1999 subtracts it. So even a quantity-1 discounted sale diverges from the stamp — these three over-report by the full discount there, while under-reporting on multi-unit lines. A fix that only adds `* si.quantity` leaves the discount half open. (ProfitRepository handles the discount separately via `saleRecognitionWeight` at :1268/:2311 — verify that arm before copying it.)

3. AUTHORITY IS STRONGER THAN STATED. The claimant listed the stamp plus five ProfitRepository lines. Add three more quantity-carrying sites: SalesRepository.ts:1872 (`SUM(si.sold_price_usd * si.quantity)` as total_revenue), SalesRepository.ts:1399 and :1413 (refund math multiplies by refundQuantity), and packages/core/src/db/migrations/index.ts:2918. That is eight quantity-carrying sites against three bare ones — the three are unambiguously the outliers.

4. NAMING PRECISION. "Closing PDF" is the checkpoint report PDF (Checkpoint/index.tsx:301-341), and since LIRA-174 the figure prints inside a rate-stamped combined USD+LBP profit block (closingReportGenerator.ts:113-122,141), not a standalone "Total Profit" line — relevant to whoever writes the guarding assertion.

5. RULE 14 NOTE for the fix: this is the exact shape rule 14 forbids — one business predicate copied into eight places. The correct fix extracts a single named SQL fragment (alongside the existing `saleFullyPaid`/`saleRecognitionWeight`/`notRefunded` fragments already used in these files) rather than patching `* si.quantity` into three more copies. Per rule 17, prove each of the three with a failing-first test on a quantity-3 line.

The finding stands. Two refinements to the write-up, neither of which weakens it:

1. NARROW THE "CLAIMED AUTHORITY". "The stamp and ProfitRepository are correct, they agree with each other" is true only for the worked example's shape — an undiscounted, fully-paid, non-partner sale. In general the stamp and `getSalesRevCost` do NOT agree: the stamp subtracts the sale-level discount (`SalesRepository.ts:530`) and adds kept change (`:553`), while `ProfitRepository.getSalesRevCost` (`:1264-1277`) applies `saleRecognitionWeight("s")` and no discount at all. Citing their mutual agreement as the authority is fragile. The durable authority is the schema plus a same-file witness: `create_db.sql:369-371` stores unit price, unit cost and quantity in three separate columns, and `SalesRepository.ts:1872` already writes `SUM(si.sold_price_usd * si.quantity)` for `total_revenue` — so the identical file multiplies for revenue and forgets to for profit at `:1999`. Any sum of these two columns that omits `* si.quantity` is wrong under every reading, independent of which reporting surface one trusts.

2. TIGHTEN THE SCHEMA CITE. `SalesRepository.ts:901-911` is the `.run()` call; the decisive evidence is the INSERT column list and its scalar cost sub-select at `SalesRepository.ts:763-767`, plus the second writer `addSaleItem` at `SalesRepository.ts:1303-1306` (which the write-up does not mention and which behaves identically — worth naming so a fix does not assume a single insert path).

Also worth adding to the ticket, since it bears on blast radius: the Dashboard tile (`FinancialRepository.ts:126-138`) and the Dashboard chart (`SalesRepository.ts:1996-2007`) carry no fully-paid gate, so the under-report is unconditional there, whereas the Closing PDF arm (`ClosingRepository.ts:868-878`) additionally requires `saleFullyPaid("s")` — the shortfall only reaches the PDF for sales that are fully settled. And per rule 14, the fix should not be three independent edits: the three sites should call one shared named margin fragment rather than each growing its own `* si.quantity`.

The finding stands; three details need tightening before it is filed.

  Dashboard "Monthly Net Profit" (FinancialRepository.ts:178-179) = 0 + 0 - 0 = $0.00

confirmed.detail: One column, two encodings. The finding stands. Four corrections:

1. LINE CITES: the History modal filter is wired at HistoryModal.tsx:38-41, not 40-43. `dateRange("expense_date")` in `getExpenseTotals` is ProfitRepository.ts:1883, not :1882 (:1882 is `activeExpense()`). `useDateRangeFilter.ts:17`, `ExpenseRepository.ts:221`, `ClosingRepository.ts:861`, `ProfitRepository.ts:2440`, `index.tsx:123` and `CarrierLineRepository.ts:907` are all exact.

2. THE HISTORY-MODAL BULLET IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE AS WRITTEN. The modal is fed `expenses={expenses}` (index.tsx:311) — the same array from `getTodayExpenses()` (index.tsx:89), already narrowed by the UTC gate at ExpenseRepository.ts:221. So (a) and (b) are never in the list at the same moment: at 01:30 local the modal holds only (b), at 10:00 only (a). The `slice(0,10)` inconsistency is genuine, but today it is masked by the upstream UTC filter; it would bite the moment the modal is fed a wider set. Drop it from the money example and keep it as a latent defect.

3. CLOSING IS TODAY-ONLY, NOT DATE-SELECTABLE. `todayLocal` (ClosingRepository.ts:56-57) hard-wires `DATE('now','localtime')` and takes no bind param. "Closing PDF for 2026-09-05" reads $28.00 only while today IS Sep 5 — the snapshot cannot be re-run for a past date through this path.

The repo's documented convention is that the business day is LOCAL (localDay.ts:1-10; ClosingRepository.ts:50-57; ProfitRepository.ts:646-663). Three of the four readers already comply. The single outlier is ExpenseRepository.ts:221, which omits `'localtime'`. Read locally, BOTH encodings land on the same local day in Beirut: '2026-09-05T00:00:00.000Z' → 03:00 local Sep 5, and '2026-09-04T22:30:00.000Z' → 01:30 local Sep 5. So changing that one predicate to `todayLocal("expense_date")` removes the entire $8/$20 flip with no data migration and no historical shift. The write-side difference is still a real rule-14 defect, but it is latent, not the cause of the numbers: local-midnight-as-UTC is only safe for POSITIVE UTC offsets — at UTC-5 the manual row would resolve to the previous local day under every one of the three local readers. Sequence the fix accordingly: (i) fix the read at :221 — that is the money fix and it is safe alone; (ii) then normalise the writers behind one named helper. Do NOT repoint the manual writer first: nothing in the closing snapshot would move today, but it would silently shift historical manual rows across `DATE(...,'localtime')` boundaries for anyone on a negative offset.

The divergence is real and operator-reachable; the money-visible symptom ($8 / $20 on the Expenses page vs $28 in the closing snapshot) is confirmed. Four corrections:

1. WRONG ROOT CAUSE / WRONG TITLE. This is not primarily a two-writer defect. It is one read-side outlier: ExpenseRepository.ts:221 uses `DATE(expense_date) = DATE('now')` (UTC day) while every other expense reader uses the shared `'localtime'` predicate — a grep for `DATE('now')` without `localtime` across packages/core/src/repositories returns that line and nothing else. Fix ExpenseRepository.ts:221 alone (use `todayLocal("expense_date")`, ClosingRepository.ts:56) and the entire worked example resolves to $28 = $28 at both clock times, writers untouched. Retitle: "Expenses page scopes 'today' by UTC day while closing and profit scope it by local day."

2. WRONG AUTHORITY. "Normalise both writers to the same encoding" is not safe and is not needed. The two writers encode semantically different inputs: the manual form supplies a calendar DATE only (index.tsx:285-287, backdatable, defaulting to localDay()), Line_Usage supplies an INSTANT with no operator date at all. Repointing manual to `new Date().toISOString()` would destroy backdating. And in the deployed timezone the encodings do not actually disagree once read correctly: Beirut is always a positive UTC offset, so under a `'localtime'` read local-midnight-as-UTC ('2026-09-05T00:00:00.000Z' → 03:00 local Sep 5) and a true instant both land on the correct local business day (verified in SQLite). The write-side divergence is therefore not independently observable after the read is fixed — it is latent, and would only bite in a negative-offset timezone. Fix the read; leave the writers alone.

3. WRONG LINE. ProfitRepository.ts:1882 is `WHERE ${activeExpense()}`; the localtime date predicate is :1883 (`dateRange("expense_date")`). :2440 is correct. CarrierLineRepository.ts:907 and Expenses/index.tsx:123 are correct.

Scope is the 00:00-03:00 local window only (UTC+3); outside it the page is correct for both row types.
